title: SAGAS: Semantic-Aware Graph-Assisted Stitching for Offline Temporal Logic Planning
claim: A reusable learned graph interface plus task-time semantic augmentation and automaton product search lets a frozen policy execute new formal specifications.
layout: 4 dashed-box modules in a loop, arrows left-to-right then back, graph inset
description: A four-module system diagram connected by thick black arrows. Bottom-left shows a maze trajectory dataset feeding upward into TD Pre-Training, which maps states (black dots) to latent states through a function psi. Next to it is Latent Graph Construction, with gray clustered nodes linked by edges. At top right, Semantic Graph Augmentation overlays red, blue and green soft-label anchor nodes and fractional label vectors on the graph. Below it, a Büchi automaton with states q0 to q4 and colored transition labels is combined with the graph through a product (×) symbol. A return arrow leads to Execution and Runtime Monitoring at bottom center. That box holds the low-level policy, a prefix/suffix high-level plan with check marks, and an eye icon for monitoring. An LTL Task box feeds in from the middle. The eye goes first to the colorful graph at top right.
caption: Overview of SAGAS. A reusable reachability interface is built from task-agnostic offline data. Given a new LTL formula and labeling function, semantic graph augmentation and B\"uchi-product search produce an accepting prefix--suffix plan, executed by the frozen low-level policy under runtime monitoring.
abstract: Linear Temporal Logic (LTL) provides a rigorous framework for specifying long-horizon robotic tasks, yet existing approaches face a trade-off: model-based synthesis relies on accurate labeled transition systems, whereas learning-based methods often require online interaction, task-specific rewards, or specification-conditioned training. We study LTL-specified robotic planning and execution in an offline, model-free setting, where the agent is given only fixed, task-agnostic trajectory fragments, with no dynamics model, task demonstrations, or online data collection. To address this setting, we propose SAGAS, a framework that combines the compositionality of symbolic synthesis with the data-driven reachability structure learned from offline trajectories. SAGAS first learns a reusable latent reachability graph and a frozen goal-conditioned executor from fragmented offline data. For each new LTL formula, it performs task-time semantic graph augmentation to ground state-defined propositions on the learned graph and applies BÃ¼chi product search to synthesize a cost-aware accepting prefix--suffix waypoint plan executed by the frozen executor. This separation of learning and planning enables zero-shot generalization to unseen LTL formulas and new predicates supported by the offline data, without task-specific rewards, additional data collection, or policy retraining. Experiments on LTL task suites constructed from OGBench locomotion domains show that SAGAS achieves higher success rates and lower execution costs than baselines on diverse unseen tasks, with further evaluation in OGBench Scene demonstrating its applicability to robotic manipulation.
